reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds table matches what Alpha reported. W2 says orders 122 and 124 were applied and 121 failed, so I'll pull the refunds table first.

The refunds table matches W2's applied list (orders 122 and 124), and failed order 121 is absent, so there is no mismatch to hold on. Next I need the customer list from the orders table before fetching each net balance.

The refunds table matches W2's applied list (122 and 124), and failed order 121 is absent, so there is no mismatch. The customers are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 31368 cents. The refunds table matched W2's applied list, so I'll continue with the next customer, birch.
Acme (31368) and birch (19998) are fetched, and the refunds table matched W2's applied list. The last customer is cobalt, so I need its net balance before recording any payouts.

The refunds table matches W2's applied list, and the net balances agree with the orders minus the recorded refunds, so there is no problem to hold on. I'll record the payouts, starting with acme at 31368 cents.

Acme's payout of 31368 is recorded. Birch and cobalt still need payouts. Their balances check out against the orders minus the applied refunds (birch 21083 - 1085 = 19998, cobalt 29756 - 5470 = 24286). Order 121's failed refund is not in the refunds table, so it is not deducted from birch, which is consistent with the ledger. I'll record birch next.

Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt's net balance of 24286 matches its orders (7562 + 22194 = 29756) minus the applied refund of 5470. The refunds table still matches W2's applied list, so I'll record cobalt's payout.

All three customers have been paid: acme 31368, birch 19998, and cobalt 24286. Each amount matched its net_balance and the orders minus applied refunds, and the refunds table matched W2's applied list. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the payout report.
